new.n: Coolidge: the 1884-91 mill town and its company vault
new.pl: Town of Fifield, on the Wisconsin Central by Coolidge Lake (GNIS 'Coolidge (historical)')
new.v: Coins 1880s, company tokens or scrip, mill and boarding-house losses
new.st: Price County history pages (WIGenWeb): W. H. Coolidge built a saw and planing mill here on the Wisconsin Central in 1884. The town had two stores, a boarding house, a post office and about 500 people. The mill ran until 1891 and the town emptied. All that is said to remain is the stone pile of the company vault in a clearing, beside a huge old lilac. GNIS keeps the site as Coolidge (historical).
new.t: Find the clearing with the lilac and the vault stones, then work outward to the boarding house, the stores and the rail siding. Check a 1938 air photo for the old clearing. Ask the landowner or the county forest office first.
src: Price County WIGenWeb history pages (recovered from the Wayback Machine)
pinev: GNIS historical point; the vault clearing itself is not yet seen on imagery.

new.st: Price County history pages (WIGenWeb): Ogema began in 1872 as 'Section 89' or Corney, a railroad boarding camp on the Little Jump River kept by Dennis McGuire while the Wisconsin Central was built north. In 1874 B. M. Holmes added a mill and a store. The village grew on the same ground. No other pin is within 0.8 km.
new.t: The camp and the Holmes mill were by the river and the mill pond (GNIS Ogema Millpond, about 600 m east). Work the old rail line and the river bank. Village lots: ask first.
